q-opening.prompt: The mist over the crossroads has not yet chosen your path. Before you take a single step -- when danger finds your company, what do you do?

options.label: I plant my feet and become the wall between danger and my friends.
options.storyLine: You plant your feet, shield raised, and let the enemy learn what it means to break against something that will not move.

options.label: I strike from where they'll never see me coming.
options.storyLine: You melt into the dark between torches, and by the time anyone thinks to look for you, the fight is already over.

options.label: I bend reality itself to my will.
options.storyLine: You raise a hand, and the world listens -- fire, force, or fate itself rearranges to suit your purpose.

options.label: I let my arrows -- or worse -- do the talking, from somewhere safe.
options.storyLine: You loose the first shot before anyone else has drawn a weapon, and you're already lining up the second.

options.label: This isn't important to me -- I just follow whoever looks like they know what they're doing.
options.storyLine: You shrug. Someone else can be the hero this time; you're just here for the road trip.

q-frontline.prompt: Your shield is raised and your resolve unshaken. When the odds stack against you, what carries you through?

options.label: Raw endurance -- let them break their weapons on me.
options.storyLine: Blow after blow lands and you're still standing, still smiling, still very much in the way.

options.label: I turn the tide with sheer force of will, calling my allies to greatness.
options.storyLine: Your voice cuts through the chaos, and suddenly your allies are fighting like they've got something worth winning for.

options.label: I bind their movements before they ever land a blow.
options.storyLine: A well-placed trip, a shove into the chasm's edge, a grapple that turns a monster's own weight against it -- the battlefield bends to your positioning.

options.label: This isn't important to me -- I'll just hit things until they stop moving.
options.storyLine: You have a plan, and the plan is "hit it again." So far, it has worked every single time.

q-shadow.prompt: Darkness is your ally. How do you turn it against your enemies?

options.label: One perfect strike, and it's over before they realize you were there.
options.storyLine: You find the gap in the armor, the half-second of inattention, and you take it -- once is usually enough.

options.label: Poison in their cup, a knife in the dark, whispers that spread like plague.
options.storyLine: By the time your target feels the sickness in their veins, you're already three streets away, sharpening the next blade.

options.label: I read a room before I ever set foot in it -- every secret is mine to know.
options.storyLine: You've already counted the guards, mapped the exits, and overheard the one lie that matters, all before the door has even opened.

options.label: This isn't important to me -- being mysterious is a full-time job as it is.
options.storyLine: You maintain an air of mystery mostly by never explaining anything, which, frankly, costs nothing and works great.

q-caster.prompt: Magic answers to you. What shape does your power take?

options.label: Fire, force, fury -- I end fights before they truly begin.
options.storyLine: You speak three words that were never meant to be spoken aloud, and the clearing where your enemies stood is, briefly, on fire.

options.label: I mend wounds and turn the tide with blessing and ward.
options.storyLine: A hand on a fallen ally's shoulder, a whispered prayer, and the wound that should have ended them simply... doesn't.

options.label: Reality itself twists at my command -- walls become doors, minds become mine.
options.storyLine: The locked vault, the sheer cliff face, the guard who was absolutely certain he'd never let you through -- none of them were ever really obstacles.

options.label: I call creatures from beyond to fight in my stead.
options.storyLine: You draw a sigil in the dust, speak a name older than the kingdom you're standing in, and something answers.

options.label: This isn't important to me -- I'll figure out what I cast when I cast it.
options.storyLine: Your spell selection process is, roughly, "point, mumble, hope." It has an alarming success rate.

q-ranged.prompt: You keep your distance -- and your enemies keep dying before they close it. What's your method?

options.label: A bow, steady hands, and endless patience.
options.storyLine: You don't need to be fast. You just need to be right, and you've had a lot of practice being right.

options.label: Black powder and steel -- the future is loud.
options.storyLine: The smoke hasn't even cleared before you're reloading, and by then everyone in the room already regrets their life choices.

options.label: I strike hard, then vanish before they can close the distance.
options.storyLine: By the time your target has decided to charge you, you're already somewhere else, and they're wondering why that hurt so much.

options.label: This isn't important to me -- point it at the loud thing, pull the trigger, repeat.
options.storyLine: Your entire tactical doctrine fits on an index card, and so far the index card has not let you down.

q-undecided.prompt: Fair enough. Let's try this differently -- when the company makes camp for the night, where do you actually end up?

options.label: Scouting the treeline, more at home under open sky than any roof.
options.storyLine: You're back before anyone notices you left, having already mapped tomorrow's route and found the one place the goblins definitely aren't hiding.

options.label: Poring over a dusty tome, chasing one more secret before sleep.
options.storyLine: The fire's died down and everyone else is asleep, but you're still squinting at a page that might just explain what that ruin was for.

options.label: Charming the last coin out of the innkeeper's pocket, for no reason but sport.
options.storyLine: You didn't need the free round of drinks. You just wanted to know you still could.

options.label: Already asleep. Adventuring is exhausting.
options.storyLine: You were unconscious before the tents were even up. Truly, an inspiration to us all.

q-complexity.prompt: One more thing, traveler -- how do you like to work? Some crave power that takes a lifetime to master. Others just want a blade they can pick up and swing on day one.

options.label: Simplicity above all -- give me a clear path and I'll walk it with confidence.
options.storyLine: You don't need seventeen contingencies. You need one good plan, executed without hesitation.

options.label: A bit of both -- some depth is welcome, as long as it never buries me.
options.storyLine: You like having options. You just don't want to need a spreadsheet to use them.

options.label: Give me every lever, every combo, every contingency -- I thrive on complexity.
options.storyLine: You have a plan for the plan's plan, and you genuinely enjoy the bookkeeping. The rest of the party finds this deeply unsettling.

options.label: This isn't important to me -- I'll figure it out around level three, like always.
options.storyLine: Your character sheet is, charitably, "a work in progress." It has been a work in progress since character creation.

q-power-source.prompt: One last thing, before the mist finally parts. Where does your strength truly come from?

options.label: A god watches over me, and I answer to their will.
options.storyLine: You've never walked entirely alone -- not really. Something older than you is always, quietly, paying attention.

options.label: No god, no master -- only the secrets I've clawed from the world myself.
options.storyLine: You bent the rules of reality through study, stubbornness, and more than a few singed eyebrows. Nobody handed you this.

options.label: The wild itself runs in my blood.
options.storyLine: Cities make you nervous. The forest never has, not once, not even the parts that are supposed to be haunted.

options.label: A loyal companion fights at my side -- I am only half of what we are together.
options.storyLine: Where you go, they go. Where they fall, you will not be far behind. Nobody who has met the two of you together doubts it for a second.

options.label: This isn't important to me -- power is power, I don't ask where it comes from.
options.storyLine: You've never once asked a follow-up question about where the power came from. This has occasionally been a mistake.
